title: Island ledgers: Threshold file
summary: Graph depth-first components. Count the numbers in the result list that are at least k (greater than or equal to k).
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
links is a square table of 0s and 1s. Points are numbered from 0. A 1 at links[a][b] joins points a and b in both directions. A 0 means no link. k is a whole number. Use it as described in the steps below.

Step 1: Build the result list
This graph has two-way links between points. A group, also called a connected component, contains all points that can reach one another. Start at point 0, then check the other points in number order. Whenever a point has not been visited, explore its whole group depth first: follow a path as far as you can before going back. Record how many points are in that group. The result list follows the order in which you first find the groups. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.

Step 2: Return the answer
Count the numbers in the result list that are at least k (greater than or equal to k). Return that count. An empty list gives 0.

Write your function
Complete islandLedgersThresholdFile(links, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.

Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
The graph has at most 16 points. Its table has the same number of rows and columns. Link entries are 0 or 1; cost entries are 0 through 13.
Efficiency goal: time O(V^2); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length; V is the number of graph points. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
hints: Try a small example by hand. Follow Step 1 and write down its result list.
